column1: # THE PORTABLE NAME PROFILE — the shared truth, and the only copy of it.
# Explained for app developers in docs/WORLD-CONSTRAINTS.md. That page describes
# this file; this file defines the rules. If they disagree, the page is the bug.
# WHY A FILE RATHER THAN A LIBRARY. Apps are Go (TinyGo -> wasm), the badge host
# is Rust, the browser host is JS. No library spans those, so "shared validator"
# has to mean one SPECIFICATION with implementations that are checked against it —
# the same shape as this repo's golden parity vectors, and for the same reason:
# two validators that agree today drift silently, and the drift shows up as an app
# that writes a file one tier can read and another cannot.
# Every implementation MUST have a test that reads this file and asserts every
# row. A new rule is added HERE first; the implementations then go red until they
# verdict is `ok`, or the error kind:
# THE RULES, in one sentence each:
#   lowercase a-z, 0-9, '-', '_', '.'      — because FAT is case-insensitive and POSIX is not
#   relative, '/'-separated                 — because a tier decides where an app's files live
#   no '.' or '..'                          — reserved for traversal everywhere
#   no Windows device names                 — the badge's files get read on a PC
#   no leading '.'/'-', no trailing '.'/'-' — Windows silently strips some of these
# --- ordinary names, which must keep working ------------------------------
# --- case: the rule with the worst failure mode ---------------------------
# On POSIX these are two files; on FAT they are one. An app that creates both
# works on a laptop and silently loses data on a badge.
# --- characters that do not survive every tier ----------------------------
# --- edges a host would silently rewrite ----------------------------------
